                             (a) Training Model Architecture                                                                              (b) Inference Model Architecture

Figure 2. Overview of the GeoDiT framework, illustrating the (a) training and (b) inference procedures. (a) During training, GeoDiT
is optimized with a mask-and-predict objective. The model learns to reconstruct the original text from a randomly masked version,
conditioned on a prompt and the visual features from a SigLIP-2 encoder. This follows a two-stage strategy: initial vision-language
alignment by training only the MLP projector (Stage I), followed by end-to-end instruction tuning of the entire model (Stage II). (b)
Inference is a non-autoregressive, iterative refinement process. Starting from a fully masked template, the model repeatedly predicts the
full sequence and then applies a low-confidence remasking strategy. High-confidence tokens are preserved while uncertain ones are re-
masked for the subsequent refinement step, a process that continues for a fixed number of iterations to produce the final output.
